claims.text: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a fine, uniform lamellar FCC/B2 dual-phase microstructure.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a room-temperature fracture stress of approximately 944–1186 MPa, or near 1.2 GPa under true-stress conditions.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has approximately 22–26% room-temperature elongation.

Cryogenic rolling followed by annealing can create a hierarchical microstructure in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 containing ultrafine FCC grains, retained lamellar regions, recrystallized FCC grains, and unrecrystallized B2 regions.
An 8% cryo-rolling reduction followed by annealing near 700 °C for 2–15 minutes will produce the proposed partial recrystallization and lamellar refinement.
Cryogenic rolling generates a high dislocation density in the alloy.
Deformation is partitioned heterogeneously among the constituent phases, producing different recrystallization driving forces.
Controlled annealing promotes partial recrystallization and grain refinement while retaining part of the lamellar architecture.
Refined grains and lamellar spacing increase the density of barriers to dislocation motion and thereby raise yield and ultimate tensile strength.
The hierarchical microstructure retains sufficient work hardening to preserve ductility.
Cryo-rolling and annealing can simultaneously enhance strength and ductility relative to as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The treated material can reach approximately 1437 ± 26 MPa yield strength, 1562 ± 33 MPa ultimate tensile strength, and 14 ± 1% elongation.
The treatment may improve strength by several hundred MPa over the as-cast state.
The strength increase will occur without a major loss of ductility.
Preserved lamellar interfaces stabilize performance under high-temperature fluctuations.
Preserved lamellar interfaces improve or stabilize corrosion performance.
Excessive deformation or annealing that eliminates the lamellar morphology may cause unacceptably low ductility.
Eliminating the lamellar morphology may degrade high-temperature stability or corrosion performance.
The treatment would make the alloy more suitable for aerospace fastener applications.

contradictions.description: The prediction permits preserved or slightly reduced ductility, whereas the falsification rule requires statistically significant improvement in both strength and ductility. A result with higher strength and unchanged or slightly lower ductility could satisfy the stated hypothesis but be classified as falsifying it.

The stated baseline elongation is 22–26%, while the cited treated-material elongation is about 14%. This conflicts with describing the treatment as a simultaneous ductility enhancement or as involving only a slight ductility reduction unless the measurements use materially different conditions.
